source_doc: Finally, I found the right ones! I was asked to find and order wind screens for the microphones in the drive-up window at the bank I work at.  I never thought it would be so difficult to find the right ones.  The mics we have are very old, so I wasn't like I could go to the manufacturers website and order replacements.  They don't make the model.  I Googled over and over and tried many different sites and searched on here.  Just measuring didn't do any good.  For one thing, the ones we had were missing the tops (did someone chew them off?) and they were stretched out, and it was hard to tell what size they really were.  I tried measuring the size of the mic and trying to figure out what would fit.  I looked at pictures, descriptions, measurements, all of it.  And I ended up with several purchases that didn't even come close. It seemed that most of what was out there was designed for lapel mics, which I guess would be very small, and gaming headsets, and most of those looked too big or two small. Finally I ordered these.  And they fit!  They seem nice, I mean they're just little pieces of foam-not much to screw up there.  Now I can quit looking and move on to the next odd thing they ask me to order.

source_doc: Medical Esthetician’s Two Thumbs Up! I am a retired medical aesthetician with a license for 20 years! Believe me I am a skin care product junkie like none other than I do have to say this mask is a game changer! It might be a teensie  bit reactive to extremely sensitive skin but I believe some of the reviews here are from people who use skin care cleansers with ammonia, Laureth  sulfate which is extremely drying so when a product that is nourishing and cold is applied to the skin it can sting! I recommend a 5.5 pH balanced cleansing bar such as the one by 100 senses  or cleanser perhaps from JLo’s line about which I can’t say much I love you, because I haven’t used her cleansers! Regardless, hyper sensitive skin that is sensitized will always sting until rebalanced no matter what you use on it.Regardless, I have been using this mask consistently  since October 2022  and it’s now March 2023 and I will say consistency is truly key and will pay off! Unlike what the instructions on the mask say I rinse the serum off after doing a facial massage and apply my own serum, but I there’s an option to leave it on all night!  If you have a normal skin that is aging a highly recommend this mask, it truly is a game changer!

source_doc: I can't believe how cheap this was. Because it certainly doesn't feel or look cheap. It looks higher end than it is.I've been using it for a little while, before deciding to write a review, and I love it just as much now as when I first got it. The keys are clacky, in a pleasing textile-ish kind of way, if you like that, but also not obnoxiously loud at the same time. I did notice the space bar is a bit springier sounding than the other keys like others have said, but I honestly don't even think about it when I'm using it anymore. The contrast of the white keys against the stainless is very aesthetically pleasing. I wish it had dedicated volume buttons, but I'll live. Because the keys are raised, I find it very easy to dust when cleaning--it even includes a cleaning brush to get between the keys, which I thought was a nice touch. The different light modes are fun, though I usually just keep them stationary. It just makes my work area a little more playful, and I love that because it's so me. I don't know much about gaming keyboards or what actually makes a keyboard a **gaming** keyboard, so maybe those who are more hardcore might be able to pick it apart. But I bet a kid would absolutely love this. I'm 38 and I sure do!

source_doc: English bully-approved. Great harness for English bullies.  Sizing is spot on, I got the large for my pups that range from 25.5-27 inches.  Quality is great too.  I do want to say that my bullies aren't 'pullers' and are pretty chill, so I can't say how durable it is in regards to more aggressive dogs.  But, I've taken them on their walks with this, and I don't feel like it may break or anything like that.  I have been using this harness for a few weeks now exclusively for one of my pups, and I haven't seen any fraying or rips on the harness.Most importantly, my pups like it.  They're pretty picky when it comes to harnesses, when they don't like one they make a point of running away when I would take ones they didn't like out, or try biting it off their bodies.  This one has passed all the tests!  One of my pups even TOOK A NAP with it on.The leash is just okay.  The handle is nice since it has the plastic piece, but I already have a leash that I like so I'm keeping this as a back up.  I mainly got this for the harness.It's a crazy good price, especially when you compare it to the name-brand ones.  This is a fraction of the price.  My pups and I are glad that I got it.

source_doc: Okay, this filter is no joke. When I first found this filter, I was skeptical. A good filter, for a 75 gallon tank, that's under $30? No way. Not when we paid $100+ for our AquaTech. I was on the phone with my husband and he almost laughed when I told him the price and that I was going to try it out. He told me not to get my hopes up, there's no way it could be good. I was doing a partial water change and I knew I'd be disturbing a lot of sediment and our old filter was on its last legs, so I decided to take a chance.Y'all. When I tell you this little thing WORKS. It cleaned my filthy tank water overnight. Within the first hour I could see a massive difference and by morning? Almost crystal clear. All the filters were filthy within a day from just how much crap they'd sucked up. Oh, and the output is so strong I had to use the little L adjuster pipe to aim the output flow at the side of the tank, because it was creating too strong of a current for my littler tetras. This thing is amazing. I'm buying another one just to put two in my tank to keep it even cleaner. Please note, I've had this thing for almost three months now and it's still going strong.

source_doc: Wonderful! I absolutely love this product! The older I get the more trouble sleeping I seem to have. For the longest time I was taking an acetaminophen nighttime formula, but I was getting concerned about taking that every day and decided that it was time to try a melatonin supplement and I am so glad that I did! Not only are the gummies very tasty, but within 30 minutes of taking two of these at bedtime, I feel the need to sleep. Although there is a small amount of sugar in these gummies the sugar does not seem to bother me, and I am very sensitive to sugar especially when trying to sleep. Not only do I fall asleep faster, I stay asleep except for the occasional times I have to use the bathroom due to an “old age” bladder.  The jar is rather big as it contains 100 gummies. Suggested use is 2 gummies at bedtime so this jar will last me 50 days if I should need to use them every night.  From the makers of Nyquil, this formula works great for me, and I plan on having these in stock at my house for as long as they do.

source_doc: Slight Odor in the Bags. I am not as impressed with this PAMI brand of gallon storage bags as I was with their quart-sized double lock bags.  There are 100 bags but NO twist ties were included with my order even though it states it on the box.  I have a ton of extra twist ties, so I moved on.  The bag is wider and shorter than my store bought ones.  So, it probably is still gallon sized.  I do like that the top is slightly uneven for easy opening.  I also like that there’s multiple suffocation warning prints on the front.Why did I give it 3 stars?  When I opened one to place prepared vegetables, I noticed a slight odor.  It’s not unpleasant or plasticky.  My store bought ones don’t have an odor.  Even though the bags are BPA-free, I decided to use it for storing non-food items, just to be safe.  For storing craft items, they are quite useful.  Each bag is about 8 cents, so twice as much as generic store-bought ones.  I would give it a resounding five stars, if it weren’t for the odor.

source_doc: Works great. I have several remote control switches and bulbs around the house.  I got this one for its small size.  I use it for my cordless phone.  I got this thing about rechargeable batteries.  I believe if you keep them on the charger they don't last long.  I have experienced this myself with power tools.  I want the batteries to last as long as possible so I charge them and then let them discharge to a point then recharge.  I am told this is not necessary but again, I have seen several devices die early on constant charge.  So I have this cordless phone on my landline and it is in a cradle and constantly charging.  I got this device and plugged the cradle into it.  When the phone  is charged, I turn off the device till it needs charging again and turn it on.  Very convenient.

source_doc: Works with all Dr. Brown Wide-Neck Nipples. I have a 4 month old baby who is quickly outgrowing small bottles. He is combo-fed. Our small Dr. Brown bottles (wide-neck) only go to 150ml, whereas he drinks 160-180ml. I had already purchased the level 2 nipples only a month ago and didn’t want those to go to waste.While these bottles come with Y-cut zippy cup nipples, these won’t work for him until 6m+. No problem there, as the level 2 wide-neck nipples I have fit perfectly. There is zero leakage and the transition is seamless. As a bonus, I will not need to buy the next size up nipples because I now have them. I ordered the vents for these bottles, as well, since my baby is very gassy and I feel he still needs them.Another reason I chose these bottles were the rubber handle on the side. My son is always trying to hold his bottle but is unable to grasp it. These handles are perfect. Right now he’s still learning, so I place his hands on the handles to show him how it works. I then hold the bottle from the end to give him support. Occasionally, I let go for a couple seconds to gauge how he’s doing.I really like these bottles and may possibly buy a couple more when he’s older and using the 6m+ nipples.

source_doc: Is okay - not good for long-term. I bought this because I wanted a clicky keyboard for when I WFH (I know - a silly reason but I prefer the aesthetic of it). It wasn't hard to set up - The mouse and keyboard function with a USB inserted into the computer/laptop and no batteries are involved. The downside to this is having to re-charge your keyboard every so often. The first time I charged the keyboard (using the cable they provided) it worked fine and I was able to use it for a couple days (maybe 3?) There's no real indicator that tells you how much battery is left - if you turn it on and the battery symbol is red that means it needs to be charged again but other than that nothing. The second time I tried to re-charge it I had plugged in the wire and had it charging for 12 hours. When I went to go unplug and use it though it was completely dead. I figured that the wire might have been faulty so I tried again with another micro-USB I had in the house that I knew worked. Still nothing. Because I couldn't replace batteries or resuscitate it really I had to toss it, which was unfortunate because the mouse was still fine.

source_doc: Just what I need. I have just gotten it all set up in our bedroom, so haven’t had a chance to really see how it is in the long run, but I am hopeful. I also have Autoimmune Dry Eye Disease, with an overlay of moderate TED (Thyroid Eye Disease), so the dryness is kind of a big deal.I got a different one last year and after I got it i went over instructions. Dear sweet Jesus, it was the most picky, intricate, PIA humidifier-thing I have ever seen. Use special water (not just distilled), and fill this other hole with whatever-the-hell (more special c**p) and be sure to run this, flip that, push this and dance around it in goatskin chaps in hopes of getting humidity.I have very high hopes for my dry, scratchy eyes, mouth so dry my tongue has to be peeled from the roof of my mouth, cracked lips, dry skin, and itchy face and hands. I haven’t had it long enough to to fall to my knees in joy and say “OMG it is the miracle I was looking for” but I bet I will in about two-four weeks.Humidity for EVERYBIDDY!!!

source_doc: Deathadder without the wire! I've tried different brands/models of mice but have cumulatively used a Deathadder for over 7 years. I've always been too scared to pull the trigger on wireless mice because I had a bad experience with one and I'm not a fan of charging things constantly but the feel, the performance, everything, is amazing. I absolutely love it! It's exactly like my Deathadder Elite but without the wire.The only thing I will say is that I was disappointed with the battery life. I game much anymore and just casually hang out on my computer on days off from work. I also have the power saving mode set to 5 minutes because I'll go AFK to clean or hang out with my dogs often, so I'm not using it a ton. I guess I just expected a little more. The product advertises a "70 hour life", which I know is on the high end, but I expected more. Overall, I love this mouse and don't mind charging it for the convenience of not having a wire anymore.

source_doc: Refused to connect. I had a lamp I wanted to use Alexa with and I have other older Kasa smart plugs that work fine.  My other bulbs were Lumiman and I thought I would try to make everything just Kasa.  So I ordered a Kasa smart bulb but it refused to connect.  I thought that maybe it was because the lamp was one of those metal swing-arm things, so I thought, well, I'll just get another Kasa plug instead and ordered a used set of 2.  They both refused to connect.  Thinking it was because they were used, I ordered 2 more new ones.  And, guess what, they refused to connect, too.  I tried everything with all of them.  Multiple tries and resets, moving the lamp all over the house and even right next to the router.  None of them would connect.  So I ordered another Lumiman bulb and, lo and behold, it connected right away with absolutely no issues.  2 stars is for the old plugs that actually worked.

source_doc: I love the thickness and double sided design of this bib. I really like this bib. In our household we go through bibs and always have a pile on hand as backups. I do love that the design is on both sides, but of course it is going to cost more. I only wish this was slightly a bit more affordably priced, but I also understand this is better quality (thickness, double sided design, etc) than most bibs, which is why it is priced at this amount. This is great for heavy droolers, especially if your little one is at the height of teething and drooling non stop. I still recommend it even if your little one is not a heavy drooler. I got this yellow safari animal design and the color is beautiful and vivid. I noticed there are also other designs available, and they are all equally adorable and have vivid colors. Overall I am very happy with this bib and highly recommend it if you can splurge a little.

source_doc: Excellent lunch bag! When shopping for some type of lunch bag item, I stumbled across the Eco-Friendly lunch bag. I liked everything I read about it so I decided to order. I cannot begin to tell you how much I LOVE it. First I was amazed how big it actually is. The depth is so nice. One of the reasons I bought this was because I needed something to keep my Grandson’s milk & juice when we are out running errands. To tell you how much you can fit in the lunch bag. I had 2 bottles of milk, 2 bottles of water and a 16 oz soda in the main section. On the inside upper lid there is a section (with a zipper to close the section off) I was able to put 2 small box juices and a small ziploc bag of grapes. If needed I could have placed more items in that section along with a outside zip storage where you can keep your phone etc. The whole inside is lined with what looks like aluminum foil that keeps items cold or hot. Also if u should spill something, all you need to do is wipe it off with a damp cloth or paper towel. To bad something like this wasn’t around when my 2 were growing up. It is so light weight and the outside material reminds me of denim. I truly believe you will love it as much as I do!

source_doc: AMAZING! It literally melts my press on nails! I’ve never been able to get professional acrylic nails because all that filing of the nail bed to prep, would traumatize my nails to the point of creating pockets of fungus. Then I discovered press on nails and with some trepidation I tried it. I took them off after three days to make sure that my nails were clean and to my relief there was no sign of trauma. A whole new world of beautiful nails  just opened up to me! I came across this little gadget and I thought I tried it. I had nothing to lose because if it didn’t work as expected, I could always return it. I followed instructions and then soaked my nails for 5 minutes. When I took my hand out I couldn’t believe my eyes! They fake nails had just disappeared! I didn’t even have to use the scrapper. I used a cotton with acetone to finish taking what little was left. Then I soaked them again for an additional 3 minutes and I was done. I rubbed tea tree oil on my nails to help with the dryness and prevent fungus. This little thing is worth every penny. Healthy nails  have no price. Now I can safely become addicted to beautiful press on nails.

I wish I had found this cover and started using it when I first bought the couch but better late than never.

source_doc: Love it! My old knob had been slipping on my genuine leather Wheel Skins cover, even though I used the optional rubber strips. I replaced this cover with a wonderfully plush, inexpensive leather-like cover. The ad for the XL spinner urged me to measure before I ordered. Out of laziness, I did not, and I had to return the regular-size knob for an XL. Installation was a bit of a hassle because the supplied small L-shaped Allen wrench had to be used upside down and out of sight. I wished I had a tool like a screwdriver handle with an Allen wrench attached. I think I did the final tightening by attaching the Allen wrench to a vice grip. I am male, but I have never been as strong as some. I love the XL knob! It operates so smoothly, like a precision instrument with ball bearings. The large, flat head provides secure, excellent control. It does NOT slip, and I wouldn't hesitate to bet it never will. This product is the cat's pajamas!

source_doc: Can I give these more than 5 stars?! I love the convenience of using a Swiffer for quick clean-ups.  I have four rescue dogs and foster frequently too so I definitely use my Swiffer a lot.  But let's face it, the Swiffer doesn't really do a great job of cleaning.  In one area of my house, I have tile that was put down years ago before it became more popular to use the larger tiles (my tiles are probably only 12" tiles so I have lots of grout).  The Swiffer doesn't seem to really get down in the grout to clean.  I bought these reusable pads mainly because I thought they would be cheaper in the long run.  An unexpected huge bonus was finding how much better they actually work than the disposable Swiffer pads!  These pads are thick and absorbent.  They make it a tad bit harder to push your Swiffer around but the results are so much better and worth the extra effort!  I haven't tried to wash them yet. I have only just rinsed them off and reused them but will wash them soon and update if I have any issues (but I don't anticipate any problem with them). They do come with instructions telling you not to use fabric softener on them - just an FYI. So glad I ordered these and I will definitely order more!

source_doc: Not for my sensitive skin. I liked the concept of this dry body brush. I thought the bristles would be much harder but they aren’t. They are softer which I thought would be a positive for my sensitive skin. It’s designed so it’s easy to hold. I initially used it as a dry brush but my skin had a bad reaction so I felt I could benefit by using it in the shower after my skin had moisture from the water. After about 10 minutes in the shower I began to use it & still my skin just didn’t like it. I brushed slowly, softly but despite the soft bristles redness was formed & I had to stop. From my personal experience I’d say this isn’t suited for sensitive skin. I feel it would greatly benefit one who doesn’t have sensitive skin. For the price it’s a nice quality brush. I would suggest, due to the nature of the wetness the bristles would get, that if you do use it in the shower that you put it in a location in your bathroom where it can fully ventilate to prevent mold.

source_doc: Great. I haven't put together many things in my life and I did this so I would say it was fairly easy. source_doc: Absolutely brilliant device. I am an instant fan of this adorable egg cooker. I found out about it only a few days ago and I am so happy I got this.To start, my boyfriend suffers from a highly sensitive egg allergy, to the point where if he's in the kitchen while someone is frying eggs he will feel unwell from the fumes. As a result, I gave up cooking eggs for myself for over 5 years.This device is a blessing because I can finally eat eggs again without worrying about bothering my boyfriend. I might not ever make fried eggs again but being able to enjoy them boiled, poached, or as a tiny omelette is more than enough for me.The domed lid keeps the "fumes" contained pretty well until I have to open it, but since all the cooking is steam powered it's really not bad. This morning I attempted soft boiled eggs and as you can see I think they turned out wonderfully. My boyfriend didn't notice any discomfort in the kitchen either.So so happy this is in my life. It's very easy to clean and I love that you can set it and forget it, since it plays a little tune when it's ready.

source_doc: Not just a pregnancy pillow! I had 2 major abdominal surgeries and was absolutely struggling to find a comfortable way to sleep. When sleeping on my non surgical side, I rolled to my belly in my sleep waking me up in terrible pain. I gave this pillow a go. I wish I’d have gotten one of these years ago! It comes vacuum packed, I tossed it in the dryer on air fluff for about 30 mins and left it out to form as suggested and washed the cover in my sensitive detergent (dried cover on very low heat because of the fabric type). It formed beautifully! I couldn’t wait to try it out. I did add a bit of extra poly fill on one side to make it more firm only because I wanted a firm barrier to prevent me from rolling on my belly. It worked perfectly! I never rolled on to my belly once. I’ve been using this all week now and I have noticed that my incision sites aren’t anywhere near as painful and it’s even helped with painful joints from fibromyalgia. I wish I could give it far more stars. It wasn’t flat like many other pillows and their reviews, it was truly perfect. This is a fantastic investment. Now I just have to work on getting the hubby to stop resenting my pillow for replacing him lol

source_doc: This is my second purchase of these. I originally purchased this belt when I had an iphone 8+ back in 2018.  I used it every other day when I ran.  I constantly pulled my iphone out of the belt 2 - 3 times a run (for pictures).  When I purchased an iphone 13 pro max I was happily surprised that it still fit in my old belt.  The belt fit me fine (I wear size 8 women's pants) and never "bounced" during the time I used it (although from time to time I did have to tighten it a bit as it sometimes came loose).Finally after many years of service, the zipper broke in December 2022.  I purchased a replacement and the quality is still as good as the original.  Not planning to upgrade my iphone any time soon, but I hope this still works in future.I highly recommend this product for those who don't like to carry their phones in their pockets when running.

source_doc: Good for kids (and very good for adults ears) These are very, very light weight. I was desperately looking for foam mallets because they just sound nicer on steel tongue drums and mid class vibraphones. I bought these, not caring that they looked like a lollypop( probably not a good thing because it may entice little ones to chew on it) So I gave them a try and even though the foam was the density that I was hoping for, the handles are so light that I can’t get the sound I want, without whacking really hard,,,,and then all you hear is the thudding and no music. I thought the handle might be hollow and I that I could somehow add some weight but the ends are sealed ( I may chop it off & see if I can add weight and then sand the ends, so they’re smooth. Hmmm….may have to update later.Pros: For parents, whose so called friends, have gotten the kiddies a xylophone, this may save your sanity…Even though the munchkins may bang away, at that thing,,,the sound will not pierce a hole in your eardrum & make you long for their 18th birthday..lol

source_doc: Seems like a good collar. My cats needed new collars and I thought I'd give this one a try.  I ordered the cloud print and it's cute.  No issues with sizing the collar to what I needed and I did try pulling apart on it to ensure it would "break away" if need be and it did come apart with a fairly good tug.  My cats are indoor cats so I doubt it will be put to the test, but would want to make sure it would just in case.  I do have to say I don't care for the bell.  My cat's last collar had a bell and it really wasn't noisy unless he was really running.  This bell is very noisy.  It's a smaller sound, kind of a tinny sound.  But I could tell my cat did not like it.  At least for the first few days he was constantly messing around with his neck like he was trying to find the bell.  He never did that with his last collar.  I was actually getting ready to take it off but it's been about a week and he seems used to it now so I'll leave it be for a bit longer and see.  But I do wonder if it's still driving him nuts.  I may still remove it at some point.

source_doc: Battery life has room to improve. I use a Glorious gaming mouse as my primary mouse. My only complaint is that I don't own the wireless version. I tried out this pwnage mouse in hopes that it would be everything I like plus the wireless aspect. In terms of customization, weight, accuracy, and feel, everything is very similar to my glorious mouse. I love it. It has a nice grip, it's very lightweight, and I can make the rgb pink. I fully charged the mouse and was gaming away until I hit about day 3 and the battery had to be recharged. Asking around my gaming group and reading online, 3 days is not very long for a wireless mouse at all. I really wish that the battery lasted longer on this mouse, but as it is I would rather deal with a cord and not have to worry about charging my mouse every 3 days. I am back to using my glorious mouse.

source_doc: Replacement to another Inspire. I had/have an inspire that is just fine except that where the band clips in, it broke and there is nothing to attach the band to. I was not going to wear the thing on my PJs because first of all I would probably lose it in the bed.  I tried another inexpensive smart watch, but the step count was really bad, and the silent alarm was one very short vibration and that was all.  So, I broke down and bought another Inspire.  I really hope this one doesn't break.  Other than that, I love this thing.  It isn't huge like most of them, and it works for what I need, counting steps and as a silent alarm.

source_doc: Pretty Good. The first time I started looking for something like this, I just gave up due to too many options.  Since I had the chance to try this, and I figured it met my first requirement of not being plastic, I was happy to give it a try.It fits the bill pretty nicely.  It saves a bit of room by getting some of the tiny stuff off the cabinet floor under my half bath sink, and then gets some of the larger bottles cleaned up and in one place as well.As I suspected, for every bit of space you gain, you also gain some complications - and I'm sure this is true for almost every device like this unless it was engineered specifically for your EXACT cabinet.For example, I like that it pulls out, but then I have to leave some space in front of it so it can do so.  And then I can't put anything too tall on the top because those things could hit the top of the door and stop it from pulling out all the way.  So it helps, but it's not making an astronomical difference under there.  I still like it.  I wouldn't bother with almost any of the plastic models.  At least this does NOT seem cheap or flimsy at all (anything cheap and flimsy trying to help you save space always makes more problems than they solve).

source_doc: Keyboard is too tall? Never thought I would have this complaint about a keyboard, but this thing is way too tall. I have had a Corsair K70 for the past 10 years and I am at a point of needing to replace it. Thought I would give this one a try and see if I liked the optical linear switches which I do really like.The problem is the actual height of the keyboard itself. It sits at least twice the height of my old mechanical keyboard. I tried adjusting my chair but found that it was a big enough difference between my mouse and keyboard that my armrests had to sit at two separate heights. Doing this hurts my shoulder and ruins my posture, but if I keep my armrests even like I would normally my wrist is bent just enough to cause pain.If you really cannot live without this keyboard for whatever reason, I would recommend raising your mousepad to match the height of the keyboard. I am tempted to do that just to keep this keyboard, but this is just dumb design in my opinion.

source_doc: It is better than i expected with a small cabinet!!! I have a sub that is a 6" that I paired with a set of Presonus Ceres 4.5BT monitors. The bass was lacking and I wanted something a little stronger. I ordered it and It was delivered in 24 hours on prime. It is much smaller than I expected. It’s just 2” deeper than the 6" cabinet it is replacing. I connected it to the system with the Presonus Ceres 4.5BT monitors. It turns on right away. And it has strong smooth bass not muddy bass. I actually had to turn it down 5-7db below 0db on the gain control to match the monitors. Now, I have a complete Presonus system, that is very impressive for the cost. I have several other systems, A KRK VXT system and a Blue Sky system this is smallest system and it is very impressive compared to the KRK and Blue Sky systems I have in head to head comparison using the Mackie Big Knob 3. Very happy with this sub. highly recommended.

source_doc: Great for Price, Better after Tweaks. Loved the lamp. I am particularly fond of the design which is why I got it. As a student moving from dorm to dorm it folds nicely. Great Student lamp. It has two different strips of lights that cause the change in color. It is not the best light I have had but for the price it is pretty decent. Lumens I provides enough light for the tasks I perform at night which are normally just computer work, occasional solder, tiny tool usage and eating at my desk. I was really annoyed with where the switch was so I cut it off and reconnected close to the base of where the clamp is. I can now easily reach the on and off and lumen adjustment. I would have preferred the switch be closer to the head or arms of the lamp but I am happy with where it is now. I added a rubber pad to the clamp so I don't get charged for damages to the desk. I also had to un hinge a spring and tighten a few of the screws. The springs are unevenly strong that it pulls the light in funky ways and after removing a few and then tightening screws the lamp still adjusts and moves and stays where I want it. I have been pretty happy with it.

I ordered a third bottle and started the drops up again and had the same positive results. This stuff is staying in my arsenal. I find that you can reduce the dose as the cough subsides. I don’t stop it anymore. I just drastically reduced it. The cough is still gone. I have little porous dental treats that my dog loves. I put the drops on those and she doesn’t mind at all. If I run out of treats, I put a couple of drops in her bowl and squirt a little bit of whipped cream on top and that does it as well. This was a miracle for us.

source_doc: No complaints with quality. I got this for an emergency pull rope / strap for the trunk of my car.. 4" did not really register as to how wide that actually is, or how thick this strap actually is, until I got it in.. One of those (brain fartt) moments where you could kick yourself in after thought.. In any case, this is way more then I need for an emergency strap, so I am going to look for another.. I have one that is thinner and not as wide in my one vehicle, and I wanted one for my other vehicle.. If you want one for something like that, this is going to be much thicker and heavier then most people will ever use..With that being said, the testing I did do with it, it worked fine.. But let me be honest when I say.. 16,000 pounds is like towing a semi.. I have nothing that will use or need that kind of a heavy duty strap to tow.. But then again, I have seen smaller one break trying to pull out bushes and stuff.. So better too heavy then not heavy enough and breaking.. Just know, if you are looking for compact, this is not for you.. But from what I can tell so far, it is nicely made and I have no complaints about its quality.

source_doc: Works well, seems well made. Ok, I hate cleaning my shower. I mean it's not gross, but it's not spic-and-span either. I was glad to receive this and as soon as I got it, I plugged in the included charger and charged it for an hour or so. (It shows a red LED when charging that flips to green when fully charged.) As the pic shows, it consists of the head, where the brushes attach, along with 2 other sections, one of which contains the battery, the other is an extension piece that also telescopes to provide more length. You also get 4 brushes of various sizes.After charging it up, I sprayed down the shower with a soap scum cleaning spray and let it sit for about 5 minutes. Then I went to town on it with this little baby. I made the mistake of trying the large, flat brush, and I quickly realized the large rounded brush is a much better option for shower cleaning. Otherwise, it's a little hard to control and it dances around a bit.It worked well, and made the job simple - no awkward bending, reaching, standing in the tub, etc. Glad I purchased it. I've not tested the battery duration yet, but it didn't slow down, and still had plenty of power after I used it.

source_doc: I should have bought this years ago. I love this thing.  I love hard boiled eggs but often don't eat them because of the hassle of making them.  When I do make them, I tend to not eat all of them, or by the time I do, they have lost their flavor.  With this egg cooker I can make them on demand with pretty much zero effort.  I also love fried eggs over medium but it's such a pain to always get out the frying pan etc... I just make medium boiled eggs with this and it's pretty much the same!  I tried doing the poached eggs, but could not find the best amount of water/time to get them cooked right.  I could get the yolk perfect, but the underside of the egg white was still runny.  Added more water and the yolk was almost completely cooked and the underside egg white was till runny.  Not a big deal because again, I get exactly the cook I want with the medium boil and can do more eggs at a time.I would have paid triple for this item it's that good.  I don't really understand the negative reviews about the timer.  It is loud, but not obnoxious and I can hear it anywhere in the house.  The melody is fine, it took me a few times to realize it was the egg timer and not my phone ringing.

source_doc: I would describe the fram brand as barely adequate, if that. The build quality feels just really cheap. Everything about it is cut rate. That's probably why it's priced right around $4 right now. I don't know about all the people that say it's destroyed their engines and whatnot. I guess that would happen if pieces came off at and it came apart in some way and started to clog up the oil passages. But from what I've seen no one's ever been able to prove that that has happened. Now that's not to say it hasn't happened I just don't have the time to do extensive research. But everything about these is just cheap. I have no idea how well they filter. For a few dollars more you can get something that feels really good quality. So I decided not to use cheap oil filters anymore and so I find these unacceptable. Like I say I'm not going to make claims that they ruin engines because I have no idea. I know the nickname for these is orange can of death. It's pretty funny but I haven't seen that to be really true at all like I said above I haven't seen proof about it. Anyway yeah I'm just not going to use filters this cheap and low quality.

source_doc: Totally worth it! So, I know you're supposed to clean the humidifier daily - that's all well and good when you're a) not disabled; b) dealing with Stage 4 Cancer ; and c) just too dang tired.  I wanted to wait and see just how well they worked before writing my review.  Each time I refilled the humidifier I would add 6-7 drops.  Normally, I clean them once a week - and I have 2 humidifiers so it takes some time to clean them.  Well, I have been very sick for 2 weeks, and I knew the chambers were probably gooky so I turned them off for about 2 1/1 days.  I cleaned them today expecting some kind of science experiment gone wrong - even cleaning them weekly I'd get a ton of gook.  Well, there was gook, but surprisingly not nearly what I expected.  I am now using 10 drops because I realized I have an almost 2 gallon tank so I'm hoping next week when I clean them I'll see even less gook.

source_doc: Very Sturdy. I have bought what feels like a ton of these over my adult life for all kinds of different, practical applications not just for hanging a shower curtain and this one has to be one of the sturdiest ones I have ever purchased.  I wasn't so sure about the black as I normally stick to white, off-white or a light tan but for the purpose of my purchase, I was indifferent because I just needed a sturdier rod in my laundry room.  I use this rod to hang the clothes right out of the dryer and sometimes, the weight of clothes can be so much that a regular, cheaper rod, will buckle under that kind of weight.  I was hoping that this rod would solve my worry about that because I had my other one fall on me, a couple of times by that buckling under the weight of the clothes.  This one is absolutely the answer.  It is really easy to install and extremely sturdy, I can easily hang about 3 loads before I have to put them in their respective closets.  That's a LOT of laundry, and an amount that my other rod couldn't even dream about holding.  The price is very reasonable as well, so if you are in the market for a really sturdy rod, this is it.  I hope you find this review helpful!

source_doc: I have thought about buying like 10 of these. I am a nail girly - I spend a lot on at-home nail products. So I have spent quite a bit on nail drills that always end up breaking. Another thing I LOVE that makes this so much better than others, is that it can go fast, but more importantly, it can go slow. Even on the slowest setting every other nail drill was too powerful sometimes, but this one is perfect. Power when you want, but gentle when you don't. I would spend $100 on this and it would still be worth it.

Thank you so much in selling me this incredible gold digger saver.

source_doc: Works great, so far. It’s very sturdy and seems well-made but I can’t speak to the adhesion, yet.  I bought this during the winter and I prefer to wait until it’s warmer so I can clean the garage floor and use the adhesive stickers for exactly where I want it.Currently I have it on an old area rug so it doesn’t slide around.  I really like how I can feel the slight elevation in the front so I know it’s close then I feel the higher back which signals me to stop.  I don’t have to guess at all; it’s like my tire fits into a perfect little trough.  I have about 3 inches between the front of my vehicle and the garage wall and maybe another 3 inches of space in the back so my garage door will close.  This device works great and saves me from guessing or getting out of my vehicle and checking clearance.  If I had one suggestion it would be that it should be a little wider but I’ve gotten use to it

source_doc: Works great for my very fine thin fragile hair, but it's a bit sticky... This TRESemmé Hair Mist Texture Mist works great for my very fine thin fragile, and somewhat curly hair. This spray mist is a bit sticky, but I guess that's what gives it its grippiness.Whenever I go out, I always wear wigs, but at home I sport the little bit of hair I have, as it's just more comfortable. source_doc: I thought I would use it more. This UV light for nails is very lightweight and as simple to use as any I've ever used. I got this for when I do my nails, so I could cure my nails all at once rather than one at a time, and it definitely works good for that when it's the finished nails. I have nerve damage in my right hand,  so I actually find that initial gluing of nail to finger works better for me if I just stick with the single nail at a time. So, unfortunately, this has only been used 1 time. I really thought I would use it more,but it's too hard for me to keep my hand straight long enough to put all nails on then under the light. I just bend them and they come off and it becomes a mess. But, having said that, it is a decent light for anyone who will not have issues like I have. Or great for even curing nail decor that needs UV light after the nails are already glue on. I wish I could have given a better review of this product, but from what I can tell, it does what it says, and works as good as it says. So I am going to give it a 5 star based off it being exactly as stated in the description.

source_doc: Bought ultra healing in lieu of regular version due to availability/pricing. Same overall quality of the ultra healing product vs the regular Curel moisturing lotion.  The former's viscosity is a little thicker, so as you apply/rub it on, there is a less fluid/liquidity feel to it as the regular Curel.  I would not characterize it as 'tackier' application feeling but definitely thicker and not as smooth/slippery.  If this bothers you, get the  regular blend Curel.  I don't have any comment (yet) if the ultra healing works any better/quicker than the regular moisturizing version as this is my first/earlier use.  I will say the regular version works fine, so I expect to have improved, quicker results from the ultra healing.  I love Curel as I have very low oil and very dry skin.  I apply the lotion in the morning and in the evening, and it resolved some significant skin cracks (actual severe that had some light bleeding) and fingertip ends very rough/dry/abrasive skin in about a week.  So now I use it regularly twice a day and have had no recurring dry, rough, or breaks in the skin.  I don't perceive either ultra or regular Curel as oily or leaving a long-standing film.  I just rub and spread it thoroughly over the skin and in a minute or two I don't even think about whether my skin is greasy, don't notice it.

source_doc: You're paying less for a reason. I've used wood glue many times. But in the past I've used gorilla glue, which has never disappointed me. I'm grateful it was only about $5 that I wasted as this will be going in the trash when I finish this. And I just purchased gorilla glue .... which I should have done in the first place.

source_doc: Inexpensive, but with cheap construction. I got this shelf/rack for my basement exercise room. It was inexpensive which is good because it is also somewhat problematically constructed.The first one they sent me had a piece soldered upside down. So I wasn’t able to assemble it. The second one had all the pieces soldered correctly but when I hung them up, the one side was longer than the other. So I couldn’t make it level. I had to Jerry rig it to make the bottom racks be level. (Second picture) I also had trouble with the mollies they included—they were super weak so I wasn’t able to successfully hammer them into the wall even after I pre-drilled holes. I got them partially in and then the top would just cave in and I had to cut them off.I found the installation instructions difficult to follow and incomplete. Thankfully I’m handy enough to figure out how to do it. But it took a fair bit of time. So just prepare yourself for that.Because it’s attached with six screws, it feels pretty solid. I think it’s going to do the job well.

source_doc: Disappointment. These are old stairs. Still though, I prepped them as I would anything that I plan to stick with adhesive. They were very easy to stick down but unfortunately they're not that sticky. I've walked over each piece on each stair back and forth multiple times to get as much pressure on every point of contact and they just won't stay stuck. I don't know what to do other than maybe some contact cement around all the edges.These are cheap and look alright. I'd be more upset if they were priced higher but I should have figured this would be the outcome for what I paid. source_doc: I love it. I did significant research before pulling the trigger on the Honbay modular sectional. I’m so glad I did. My family and I absolutely love it. As other reviews mentioned, 5 out of 7 boxes arrived earlier than expected. The 2 remaining boxes arrived the next day. I love the storage in each piece, which really helped to declutter my living area and eliminated the need for two storage baskets, freeing up floor space in the process. I love the firmness of the seats. I would agree with other reviews that the back cushions could be fluffier but I added a lot of my own pillows which solves that problem for me. My kids and my dog have bounced around on it and I haven’t noticed any instability. With the layout I chose, I love the little cutout which makes it easy for kids or dog to climb in. I’m so thrilled with my new sectional. If you are on the fence, do it!!

source_doc: Good Keyboard for a Beginner or Novice. this is a nice keyboard for beginner.  It's not quite the full piano keyboard size but better than a 66 key offered on some. I have noticed that the keyboards and the song playback option are just a bit off.  One or the other is sharp or flat by just a little so it is a bit annoying.  I went with Yamaha because of the name and the PSR-EW310 is near the bottom of their price range, and I am glad I bought it.  It does not include a stand or a bench but the small table I have it on works fine for now, no sustain peddle either.  I did buy some headphones because I live in an apartment and so glad I did because it helps shut out other noises and I can concentrate better.  Yes, I'm a little ADD.

source_doc: Wow was I surprised when I opened this! I purchased this but thought maybe I should have bought glass instead. When I saw it it looked so much like glass and even felt and sounded like glass. It wasn't just me I bought one as a gift for someone else and she couldn't believe it was not glass either but best of all, it fell off the counter the other day. I was sure it would crack or something. Instead it bounced! That sucker hit the ground hard on a hardwood floor and not even a scratch. I don't know about the floor though LOL! I highly recommend. If you're going to make triple layer cakes go for something a little taller but it is great for a double layer cake and I use lots of fluffy whipped cream icing. Fits right over the top and I also cover the bottom with the cardboard cake rounds. I don't know if that's necessary but I figure if I ever want to use the bottom as a charcuterie tray I don't want to mix my meats and cake so as a precaution I use the cake rounds. Excellent item!

Read the notes of the perfumes, from this creator, to find one that suits you, and I’m sure you will, I know I will most certainly be purchasing more. Thank you for such a heavenly fragrance.

source_doc: Not the best for spices. I bought these to store some of my dry spices however I noticed that the jars had a strong chemical smell when opening them. I did not want these chemicals to seep into my spices. After a bit of tinkering with the jars I realized that the chemical smell was coming from the white styrofoam seals in the lids—once I took them out the jars smelled fine. I choose these jars specifically because they screw shut unlike some others jars that just have a cork/plunger type lid. For my purposes since I use my spices frequently and I don’t live in a very humid climate I don’t need the airtight seals which I took out. With that in mind this was a good purchase for me however it may not be for others who are looking to store spices.Edit————After removing the chemical smelling seals that came with these jars I decided to buy rubber gasket seals online to replace them. Cheap and very effective and now my jars are air and water tight. Unfortunate that I had to go to this extra step but these jars are nice enough for me to go the extra mile.

I work from home and have a couple of dogs a toddler and various other distractions around the house, usually when I want to tune them out I throw on some headphones but sometimes I just want quiet so I got these to help with that.  It came packaged well and I didn't see any defects in them.  In the box you get a case, two rings to put the ear tips on, and 6 different ear tips to use.  I chose the large double-flanged and got to it. Getting the stock tips off was fairly easy and putting the new ones on was too after that I stuck them in.  It isn't complete noise cancelation I can still hear most things fine but it's like the volume got turned down a bit which I love.  Also when Im wearing them I can barely feel them so I might actually try sleeping in them.  All in all, these are fantastic 5 starts not notes.

source_doc: Simply Beautiful. I got these lights in with no idea of what exactly I was really ordering. Which is very odd for me because I don’t spontaneously get products without reading every little detail. When they arrived and I saw that the strand was 400’ long,  I was surprised and then a little disappointed in myself for ordering them. Until my brain started to click. I decided to take the forever long, flexible and sleek looking strand and I literally wrapped each branch of my Christmas tree from the top to the bottom and still had plenty left over. They were so pretty, blended right in and had people asking me if my tree was a pre lit. I didn’t have to worry about gaudy light string’s being seen, lights never got hot and I was able to change them from being on steady to blinking, twinkling or fading in and out. I also loved how it came with a remote control as I was able to change the brightness level. I do recommend that If you do use these and decide to wrap them up afterwards, take your time and go slow or you’ll end up with a big birds nest as I did. I was able to get it straightened out but it took some time!

My boyfriend is an electrician, and I am hoping he can help ease this process and make it worry free for me… but for now, I’m not so sure what to do. There are detailed instructions, but I am scared to do something wrong… and how do they connect between cabinet spaces? However, I am happy this came with all the pieces necessary for the job. And as you can see the lights actually work and are pretty bright. I can’t blame the lights that I don’t know how to install… but to me, personally, it’s not very user friendly. I “pretend” hung them in my kitchen, and they weren’t long enough any way. I would consider hanging them in my closet, where no cutting would be involved, but I don’t have an outlet in there. Hopefully one day I will be able to provide an update with a more positive review.

source_doc: Going back to knipex. Long story short, I tried to use these, and they weren’t for me. After cutting what turned out to be a hot wire thanks to sloppy wiring in the past, I discovered these after watching a video recommending them.  I thought the pliers would be sort of a two tools in one for my tool belt.  If I need to cut a heavy gauge wire, the button would give me additional leverage without going back to my tools or carrying one more tool around.  What happened instead was the 85% of the time I was just cutting 10, 12 or 14 ga romex that the pliers were awkward in my hand and about half the time locked shut.  It would turn  a no look grab from tool belt, cut and return to tool belt into a grab, fiddle, cut, return.  I don’t have small hands but I am certainly not palming basketballs either (typically size L glove). The wihas were bulkier than my knipex cutters. The difference was a tool that took little thought was replaced with a tool that just didn’t fit or feel right.  When I was removing some old chain link fence, I appreciated the extra leverage but how often do I do that.After trying them for a month, I finally just went back to my knipex cutters.  Maybe I didn’t give these a fair shake, but I really don’t like using tools that offer me no benefit.

source_doc: Awesome thermometer. I love this thermometer! I never worried about a thermometer until the RONA hit. The first time I caught it was right before we could get vaccinated and I have Fibromyalgia so even the CDC told us that I was going to have a rougher time of it than my mom. And I did, I fought with a fever for over a week while she never had a fever. (That's just the pertinent symptom here) We had gotten 2 thermometers one for the temple and I got a regular one because I had to be able to use it simply and in the dark and didn't want to fumble with it. But they both used button batteries. Guess what, a couple years later when I got it a second time (proving I was more prone to it because I didn't pass it to my mom as she had passed it to me) Both thermometers were dead and we couldn't check my temp, though I didn't have a fever. So when I saw this one and saw it took normal every day run of the mill always on hand batteries and that it displayed the same as the ones we had I grabbed it right up and it didn't disappoint. And while I don't need it yet, I did try it and it works perfectly. I'm so happy with this thermometer.

source_doc: Great bulbs! I had a lamp I wanted to use Alexa with and I have other older Kasa smart plugs that work fine.  My other bulbs were Lumiman and I was thinking I'd switch to all Kasa so I'd have just the one app on my phone.  So I ordered a Kasa smart bulb but it refused to connect.  I thought that maybe it was because the lamp was one of those metal swing-arm things, so I decided I'd just get another Kasa plug instead and ordered a used set of 2 minis.  They both refused to connect.  Thinking it was because they were used, I ordered 2 more new ones.  And guess what, they refused to connect, too.  I tried everything with all of them.  Multiple tries and resets, moving the lamp all over the house and even right next to the router.  None of them would connect.  I thought it was me.  I decided last resort to try a Lumiman bulb just to eliminate a Kasa hardware factor and maybe my WiFi was an issue and, lo and behold, it connected right away with absolutely no issues.  Plus, these have no color which I rarely use on any of my smart bulbs.  So win win.  Too bad it seems there are no Lumiman plugs.  I used the second bulb in a lamp where I was using a Kasa plug.  Anyone have any recommendations to replace my other Kasa plugs?

source_doc: if you use festool, with makita vac…it’s a must. it has taken me a long time to work with multiple tool platforms. No it’s not the festool system, but it works for me and has made my desire to get another dust extractor not be a hot button issue.  The older I get the more conscious I am of what I am breathing in.  I can’t say I gave much thought into sanding walls in my fraternity house 30 yrs ago. What I can say is that while I work alone in a job, I will have several extractors, but as far as I am concerned this hose has at least temporarily saved me $900.

source_doc: Best Wipes - From a Preschool Teacher! I’m very fortunate in that I teach a class of twelve toddlers who all require diaper changes throughout the day. I’m fortunate because while I was pregnant, I was able to test out ten different kinds of wipes! These were by far my favorite. Most wipes are too dry to really get anything clean. I felt like I was scrubbing some of the kids’ bottoms to get them clean, which obviously isn’t very comfortable. These wipes are a dream! Wet enough to get the job done, and thick enough that I have never felt like I was going to get anything on my fingers. (Granted, I wear gloves at the preschool. I mean with my new daughter!) My girl has never had diaper rash, and while she has eczema on her little face cheeks, her booty remains clear! I had 3 boxes of these wipes, and she is ten weeks old. I still have 3 packs from the second box, and I’m only opening the third to send some to daycare. They last a while! Just get them!

source_doc: Took me a long time to figure this out, but happy with it now. I was eager to try this as a way to record from my guitar onto a Macbook Pro, but was totally new to this type of device.  I understood that I would need to download 'digital audio workstation' (DAW) software, so I read about a few options and decided to go with the free version of Waveform. After downloading it, and connecting my guitar to the BOMGE, and connecting the BOMGE to my laptop (all of which were simple and quick), I spent an unsuccessful hour trying to achieve a recording. Then I downloaded Audacity software and retried, but was again unsuccessful. At that point, I had no idea whether the trouble was the BOMGE or just me not being able to figure this out. Turned out it was me. I returned to Waveform, re-watched a couple of its Youtube tutorials (which I highly recommend for beginners), and eventually got the hang of this. (With the guitar plugged into port 2, make sure that the 'inst' button is set on, and in Waveform, set the input for the recording track to 'input 2.') After that, the info page that came with the BOMGE was meaningful, and I have found the device to be just what I hoped for. It is compact in size and provides a fine sound quality for my amateur level.

source_doc: The formula has changed. I bought this product because I have used it before and loved it.  However something changed and it caused a mild allergic reaction.  I know that I have some allergies that often get labeled as “fragrance” in skin products so I normally test a new product on my wrist first.  I didn’t this time because I had used the product before, so I just immediately applied it to my whole face. I did notice that the scent was stronger and the ingredients have changed slightly (I looked after I had the reaction).  I normally would not leave a negative review on a product for an allergic reaction, but since this was something that I have been able to use without issue in the past and can no longer use, I felt that people should know.

source_doc: Really liked them, but they would not charge. I really liked these lanterns. They flashlight option was extremely bright. The big downside is the charging. Upon receiving them, I plugged them both in. A blue light came on for about 5 seconds and then disappeared. I assumed this meant that they were fully charged. I took them camping and they started fading before the end of the first night. The next day I plugged them both in for about 3 hours apiece. The same thing happened when I plugged them in, a blue light for about 5 seconds then it disappeared. No indication if they were actively charging or fully charged. After 3 hours of charging apiece, I tried using them for my 2nd night of camping. As soon as I turned them, they died within a minute as if they hadn’t been charged at all. I returned them. These lanterns failed me on my camping trip. I can’t have an unreliable light source that doesn’t given any indication at all of charging or battery status. It’s a shame because I really liked the outside of the charging issues..

Only time will tell if this will hold true for me, but it probably doesn't matter because I can just replace the switch and keycaps when this dies, unlike the GPRO TKL (you can desolder it...).

It’s not worth the high chance that it will be defective.

source_doc: The shrimp are healthy! The shrimp are beautiful and healthy and so fun to watch.  DO NOT put them in a tank with a betta, guppies or Harlequins.  I have 2 tanks, and at first, I thought it was the betta that was eating them, so I removed him to my second tank. They still kept disappearing, so I removed the harlequins, because after hours of observation, I saw them get aggressive to the helpless shrimp. All that was left was guppies, and they still got eaten. I loved the shrimp so much, they were so fun to watch, but if I try again, I will have them in their own tank with nothing else.  They all arrived alive, healthy and very active.  Their color is so striking.  I feel terrible the research I did online was wrong.  I do wonder if you can keep different colors of shrimps together?  The red and white ones are so cool, too.  So learn from me, people, and don't put them with other fish or they will become a very expensive appetizer!

source_doc: 1mg time release lasts WAY too long, 13+ hrs after taking pill. I've done a lot of experimenting with different timing/dosage of melatonin, so I have a pretty good sense for how any given pill is affecting me. In theory, a 1mg time-release pill should be exactly what I need (more on this below). However, for me, this pill takes too long to kick in, and then induces drowsiness WAY too long. I don't feel much affect until 1-2 hours after taking it, and then it gets most intense right when I need to be waking up (about 8 hours in), and then it continues to make me sleepy for 4+ hours after that. I can definitely feel the affects lasting more than 12 hours.Before trying this tablet, I had been taking a regular melatonin pill divided into 0.5mg pieces twice per night---0.5mg before bed, and 0.5mg between sleep cycles (about 4 hours later). I had been doing this because I need help both falling asleep and staying asleep, and I only need a little melatonin to notice the affects. Taking 0.5mg twice worked well for me. Then I discovered this time-release 1mg tablet, which sounded ideal since I wouldn't have to take a second dose halfway through the night. However, this pill takes too long to kick in, and then lasts WAY too long after that (as described above).

source_doc: Nice kit with plenty of extensions. I used this to pull the center drive shaft bearing on my BMW. I found it really easy to setup and get everything in place. I had to use a pair of extenders to reach down the shaft a ways, but even with them combined I found that the tool worked perfectly.All of the pieces are well made and precisely cast. There is a pretty sharp edge to the bearing separator that is great for some applications. This tool is made of cast metal, but it's stronger than I expected.The case is great also at keeping things organized.This is my first tool from Orion Motor Tech, but I'm happy enough that I'll look for their brand next time.Update 02/20/23...I have now used this to remove 5 different bushing or bearing sets and I'm Really Really happy with it. The last bushing I removed was the lower control arm bushing and I used a low torque impact wrench to turn the shaft instead of my fixed ratchet. No matter what I throw at this tool it remains looking and working like brand new. If I lose this one day I would buy it again. Of course I can't imagine it breaking at this point, but I would buy it again in that case as well.

source_doc: I'm REALLY Impressed. At the beginning of pandemic, I was constantly on video calls/doing virtual presentations etc. I heard a lot of  other people in meetings where you could barely understand them, and decided that I didn't want that to be me. I decided to buy a Blue Yeti because I figured it's probably important that other people can hear you speaking.After a few months, I upgraded to the Shure SM7B. It was an incredible upgrade and I was very happy with it. If you can, start with the Shure as opposed to a USB mic.Fast forward a few years, and I'm doing meetings and hosting webinars at least once a day. I heard the Neumann U87 is what NPR uses and I wanted to up the professionalism. I couldn't stomach paying $3500 for a U87, so I decided to compromise and get the TLM 103. It's a huge step up from the Shure.Both are great, but the 103 is way less fuzzy and sounds a lot more like my actual voice. A bonus, is that now I don't have to use a $150 cloud lifter to get decent sound out of the Shure. I highly recommend this product. The price is still a kick in the teeth, but it's noticeably better than anything I'd tried previously.

source_doc: Everyone said I was dumb for getting this. Literally everyone I spoke to who mentioned this type of product wrote it off and said it was unnecessary and I was dumb for wanting it. I just swipe a glop of jelly onto it before the change and then smear it on my baby’s bottom like icing on a cake. The flat sides are great because you can get jelly right in the crack without hassle. You can also tackle their legs and arms without worry of getting them messy with jelly. It is easy to clean with a baby wipe after as well

source_doc: Using as an Ice Bin. I am writing this review and including pictures for those, like myself, who wants to use this as an ice bin.  I don't have a refrigerator with an built in ice maker and so I needed something to store a bag of ice.  I had originally purchased the 21 cup LocknLock but when it arrived, it didn't look big enough to hold a big bag of ice; so I sent that one back and ordered this 50.7 cup LocknLock bin.  It is large and takes up almost half to the upper freezer shelf but as I have a separate stand alone freezer, this isn't a problem.  What I like about it is that this bin have a large front door that I can scoop ice out of.  The lid snaps easily in place and the base seems pretty solid so I don't expect any leakage.  No cons so far but will update if I experience any.  The pictures shown are what was left of the bag of ice I'd purchase, so about a quarter of the bag.  I think another bag of ice will fill this bin completely full.

source_doc: Feels SO wonderful on my scalp! I have kinky/coily 4b/c hair. I have routinely oiled and massaged my dry scalp with my fingertips 2-3 times per week. I just received my massagers and washed my hair yesterday. Because my kinky/coily hair is VERY difficult to detangle when wet, I did not use while shampooing (YET! I plan to try that later). I wanted to try it 1st with my regular routine - oiling and massaging my dry hair. I began massaging 1st with my fingertips (as usual), then immediately switched to my new silicone massager. The feeling on my scalp was instantly different and wonderful. The massager felt so much better than my fingertips!  I finished at 5:10pm, it is currently 6:10pm and my scalp is still tingling from the excellent blood circulation results of the massager. NEVER felt this when used only fingertips. Also, I saw that one person gave a low rating, stating that the massager hurt scalp and tangled hair. I massaged my scalp gently and it felt SO GOOD! I also noted that, as with fingertips, I always have to detangle with my fingers after massaging. After using massager, my detangle process was about the same and actually seemd a little easier. I love the massager! I will send an updated review if/when I try on my wet kinky/coily hair.

source_doc: Meh... It's OK for low volume playback. So, I have 2 offices I work out of in my home. My small office has a set of M-Audio AV32.1 to play background music at low volume, but I always find the low end lacking. I run a 10" Monolith sub in my other office, paired with Mackie XR624 monitors and I'm mostly happy with that setup, so I thought I would get another Monolith, but I think if would be way too much sub for the M-Audio speakers. Thankfully, Monoprice makes a very inexpensive 10" sub that supposedly plays down to 20hz. I played with it for a couple of hours, and so far, it's ok. I'm cycling now to break it in, but overall it adds that little depth  I was missing on the M-Audio speakers. I'm sure they'll sound better once they are broken in. I'm still on the fence about this sub, since it lacks authority like the Monolith or the 15" DR. HSU I have for my main setup.  Then again, I haven't added a proper crossover to the small office setup, so the verdict is still out...  For small room, low volume - I give it a 3 out of 5.  If you can afford it or wait for a closeout, the Monoprice Monolith 10" is 10 x better.

source_doc: Good value. I bought this in January, 2023 and have been playing it for 3 months now. I am a beginner so I didn’t want to invest too much in something if I didn’t stick with it. The threads aren’t rounded off but don’t stick out too much on the sides. The strings were a bit rusty from the warehouse but I didn’t change them out in case I wanted to return. I finally changed them out the other day after 3 months averaging 8-9 hours a week of playing.  Sounds much brighter and louder now with fresh strings. The tuning pegs turn smoothly and after the strings stretched they hold tuning fairly consistently. I decided it was time to get it a case and today received this case today. A perfect fit. Crossrock Hardshell Arch Top Wood case fits OM, Martin 000 Guitars-Vinyl Tweed(CRW600OMTW)If you’re a beginner, I think this is a good one to go with. I really like the tone of it compared to others I have heard. My music interests are Dixieland and music from the 30’s so the tone fits that era well.

In the past, I had always associated waxing with pain, but with this device, I barely felt a thing.One of the things I loved most about the roll on wax device was how efficient it was. The wax came off of the strips and the device itself with minimal effort.In conclusion, I highly recommend the roll on wax device to anyone looking for an effective, painless, and efficient hair removal method.

source_doc: I hesitate to say how much I love this guitar but…. I sent mine back. It was said to have a blemish on the body. It did not. It was gorgeous and beautiful and I love the feel and pickups. It had a warped neck. It needed a fret job and a nut job. I can do fret jobs but I can’t fix a warped neck. I almost cried sending it back. It had a wonderful vintage feel and tone. I plan to get another. I love this guitar and I have a lot of guitars. I can’t recommend this to anyone other than luthiers who appreciate the 70’s.To new players get a new guitar with perfect action and half price. Eart. There’s so many.

source_doc: Engine power is reduced? This can be your fix. Ok, another Cadillac story, it has been showing "engine power is reduced" for as long as I got the car as a gift. I don't mind to work on it, and for 2 months I learned a lot. I programmed all the modules that I replaced, still, engine power is reduced...So the last two things I was going to do was to change the fuel, then change the accelerator pedal, since I already changed the throttle body, the accelerator pedal was one big thing on the DTC report. My friends thought I was wasting my money, since how the Accelerator pedal can cause that? Well, that part was under water...so...why not? I took my old pedal out, to my surprise it was really easy to get it out, basically just one screw! Then I opened it, it had some corrosion on it, I tried to clean the chip with contact cleaner and wire brushes, didn't work. So I waited till next day this delivered, replaced it. Turn on the car, the "engine power is reduced" message is gone!! I ran GDS and it didn't show any DTC code, so this was a successful fix!

source_doc: Absolutely Luxurious. I have been singing the praises of Andy Pandy diapers for six years and you could not have paid me to use anything else. Until the size large were out of stock for months. I had no choice but to find something similar and I did when I came across Eco Boom. Then for a reason I cannot recall I was on the hunt again. These diapers were on sale and oh how I wish I had been able to purchase more because they are the best diaper I have ever put my hands on. The feel absolutely divine, almost too good to be something a little human poops on. I have had no issues with leaking and they hold pee just as well as the other bamboo diapers I have mentioned here. They are out of my price point but if I they ever go on sale again I will be back. If you can afford them, I highly recommend these diapers.

source_doc: Its ok. not great, but not terrible. I looked at almost every bedside bassinet on market. Read every review, and ended up getting this one. Its not bad. its ok. I dont see much of an issue with sturdiness like some report. I think if you push with force any object even a livingroom couch you can get it to teeter totter. I think the collapsable feature to fold up and set back up is not as simple as i had thought. I wish i had watched a video of someone doing both. I imagine we will leave it assembled and just pick it up to go to another room if needed. The height has 4 settings, although not as high as i imagined. it wont even line up flush with our basic bedframe and matress i think is low to begin with, sits lower. For what it is and for the price, i cant imagine any other would be any better. So, for now, it may work out. baby not here yet, so havent actually used it yet.

source_doc: Very convenient way to work on my bike. This repair stand has made working on my bike much easier.  My back is not what it used to be, so I prefer to sit when working on my bike.  I used to flip my bike over and balance it on its handle bars and seat to perform maintenance and repairs.  Now I just clamp it in and go.  I can work on the derailleurs so much more effectively now that it can be upright instead of upside down.  I do not have an e-bike so I am not sure if it would handle that weight.  My bike is about 58lbs to give you and idea of what I have been using this stand for.  The tool tray has magnets that are great for holding the little nuts and bolts that have to be removed.  The tray is sturdy enough to hold my commonly used tools, but I would recommend not putting too much weight on that particular part.  The clamp has been kind to my bike's finish and has not scratched it at all.  I don't fold the stand up very often because I have enough space not to worry, but I do like having the option.  It folds up easily and is pretty compact.  I recommended this to anyone that prefers to do their own bike maintenance.

source_doc: Great for the price. I found myself DIYing a new stereo install in a 2015 Miata.  The Mazda engineers seem to have intentionally made everything difficult to get to, or super tight to work around for anyone with big hands.  I ordered this because I don't forsee myself doing much of this sort of thing, so I didn't want to invest in a "I do this for a living" quality product.The plastic is kind of soft, so I don't imagine these would manage to survive much more than a dozen or so cars worth of stereo installs, but for the money it sure as heck beats the more durable options.I didn't even realize it comes with valve stem caps when I ordered it.  That seems like an odd inclusion, but I suppose if I ever need to fill up with air at the gas station and manage to forget to put the cap back on, at least I have spares (enough to derp every wheel twice!)If you're looking for something quick and dirty to accomplish a task, and not looking for something to earn a living with, these are just fine (and heck, for all I know the more expensive ones are just as durable, and I owe these guys an apology)

source_doc: I love this thing! This product came and it was exactly how I expected it to come. Shipped perfectly! This thing works great, and has a mind of its own (in the best way). I usually like to run it when I am at home, just incase it gets stuck or anything, but it also runs while I’m at work! Which is awesome because it makes the house feel a little bit cleaner when I get home and takes the stress off a little bit. I like to use this in between vacuums too, and I can’t believe how much it picks up even right after I use my vacuum! I would recommend this to pretty much everybody, especially pet owners with a dog who sheds, like me! Great product! The app is so easy to use and I can start the cleaning or pause the cleaning right from my phone, from anywhere! I don’t have to be home to operate it which is another added bonus! Plus it alerts you if the vacuum is stuck or has low battery.

И это здорово, потому что, когда я прихожу домой, в доме кажется немного чище, что немного снимает стресс. Мне также нравится использовать ее в перерывах между уборками обычным пылесосом, и я просто поверить не могу, как много она собирает даже сразу после того, как я пропылесосил/а обычным! Приложение настолько простое в использовании, что я могу начать или приостановить уборку прямо со своего телефона, откуда угодно! Мне не нужно быть дома, чтобы управлять им, что является еще одним дополнительным бонусом! Плюс оно предупреждает вас, если пылесос застрял или у него разряжен аккумулятор.

source_doc: Well made, good value. This one I am keeping. I have purchased other guitars with semi hollow jazz style design. I have gotten rid of all of them, mostly because of feed back and tunning issues. I did spend a lot of time getting the action to my liking. At first I thought I would not be able to accomplish this but I got it. I was tempted to buy the classic vibe model because I already have one in 50's tele, which I really like. However, I really like the simplicity of design on the affinity model in spite of some of the bad reviews I have seen. Did not really find them on this guitar. The neck set up was a bit of a challenge but I got there. I also own an American made tele and strat. Nothing plays as easy or as well as those. This one poses a good competitor at a really substantially lower cost and it is really pretty, The pups are not the greatest but still really ok and I can refine the tone with my modeling style amp. I truly enjoy playing this guitar.
